title: Tissue Clearing and 3D Analysis of Dopamine Neurons in Developing Mouse Midbrain
author: Adolfs, Raj, et al.
materials: Isolation and fixation of embryonic (E12-E19)/postnatal (P0-P10) ACTB-Flpe:Pitx3-ITC brains. For adult brain, we recommend use of the iDISCO protocol with perfusion (Renier et al., 2016; https://idisco.info/idisco-protocol/) instead of the 3DISCO protocol.1.Brains are isolated in 1× PBS using a dissection microscope.2.After brain isolation, the meninges must be removed to allow better antibody penetration.3.Brains or whole embryos are fixed in 4% PFA in PBS (pH 7.4) without rotation at 4°C overnight (approx. 16 h).4.The next day, PFA is removed and 1× PBS is added.CRITICAL: Do not fix brain tissue longer than recommended. Immunostaining can otherwise be compromised due to excessive cross-linking of proteins.Note: For the analysis of embryos up to E15.5, whole embryos can be processed using this protocol depending on the quality of the primary antibody used. The anti-GFP antibody used here (Invitrogen) does not work effectively in whole embryos or in isolated brains with meninges. Therefore, when GFP immunostaining is required isolated brains without meninges are used for experiments, even for embryonic tissues (E13.5). For the analysis of E16.5 and older samples, brains are isolated from the embryo or pup.Pause point: Brains can be stored at 4°C in 1× PBS for one week. For longer storage, add 0.01 % Thimerosal to the PBS.

steps.title: Prepare PBSGT buffer
steps.instruction: Make 1 L of PBS‑Gelatin‑Triton X‑100 (PBSGT) by adding 2 g gelatin (0.2 % w/v), 5 mL Triton‑X‑100 (0.5 % v/v) and 0.1 g thimerosal (0.01 % w/v) to 1× PBS (pH 7.4). Dissolve gelatin at 37 °C with regular shaking until fully dissolved. Store at 4 °C; solutions containing thimerosal (or 0.01 % sodium azide as alternative) are stable for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Collect embryos and isolate brains
steps.instruction: Using a dissection microscope, isolate embryonic (E12‑E19) or post‑natal (P0‑P10) brains in 1× PBS. Remove meninges to improve antibody penetration.

steps.title: Fix brains overnight
steps.instruction: Fix brains (or whole embryos) in 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) prepared in PBS (pH 7.4) without rotation at 4 °C for ~16 h (overnight). The next day, discard PFA and replace with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Store fixed tissue (pause point)
steps.instruction: Brains can be kept at 4 °C in 1× PBS for up to 1 week. For longer storage add 0.01 % thimerosal to the PBS.

steps.title: Block tissue
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample in PBSGT blocking solution at room temperature on a horizontal shaker set to 70 rpm. Follow Table 1 for incubation length (E12: 3 h; E13‑18: 24 h; P0: 36 h). Use 2 mL of blocking solution per sample in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Discard blocking solution and add primary antibody mix: sheep anti‑TH (1:500) and rabbit anti‑GFP (1:1000) diluted in PBSGT + 0.1 % saponin. Incubate on a horizontal shaker at 37 °C, 70 rpm, for the times listed in Table 1 (E12: 3 days; E13‑18: 2 days; P0: 10 days).

steps.title: Wash after primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample to a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 15 mL PBSGT. Rotate at room temperature for 1 h. Repeat this wash six times (minimum 1 h each).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody solution: donkey anti‑sheep 568 (1:750) and donkey anti‑rabbit 647 (1:750) diluted in PBSGT + 0.1 % saponin; filter through a 0.20 µm filter. Incubate the sample in 2 mL solution in a dark 2 mL Eppendorf tube on a horizontal shaker at 37 °C, 70 rpm, protecting from light. (If conjugated primary antibodies are used, skip this step.)

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample to a dark 15 mL Falcon tube with 15 mL PBSGT. Rotate at room temperature for 1 h. Perform six consecutive washes of at least 1 h each. Samples can be stored in PBS at 4 °C for up to 2 days.

steps.title: Convert light‑sheet files for Imaris
steps.instruction: Drag the first file of each Z‑stack (Z0000) into the Imaris File Converter to create an .ims file. Save the converted files on a local drive to speed up later analysis.

steps.title: Open dataset in Imaris 3D view
steps.instruction: In Imaris, open the .ims file and select Surpass > View > 3D view (or press Ctrl+5). Use rotation, Slice Viewer (Ctrl+1) and Section (Ctrl+2) functions to inspect the sample for damage, antibody penetration, focus, or motion artefacts.

steps.title: Create manual TH surface
steps.instruction: Add a Surface (3D view > Surface). In the wizard choose ‘Skip automatic creation, edit manually’ and deselect ‘Volume’. Switch the camera to Orthogonal mode. In the Draw tab, select ‘Click’ mode, set pointer to ‘Select’, then to ‘Draw’. Draw the TH‑positive boundary on selected slices (skip 5‑20 slices where the shape does not change). Use ‘T+left click’ to adjust points. After completing all slices, press ‘Create Surface’.

steps.title: Place reference frame
steps.instruction: Add a Reference Frame (3D view > Reference Frame). Move it with Ctrl+right‑click and rotate with Ctrl+left‑click. Align the frame to consistent histological landmarks: midline of ventricles for medio‑lateral, upper edge of ventricles for dorso‑ventral, most caudal TH point for rostro‑caudal. Enable visible planes in xy, xz, yz to verify alignment.

steps.title: Mask Citrine channel to TH surface
steps.instruction: Select the TH surface, choose ‘Mask Selection’, then pick the Citrine channel. In Mask Settings set ‘Constant Inside/Outside’, enter 0.000 for ‘Set Voxels Outside Surface to’. This creates a new masked Citrine channel. Open Display Adjustment (Ctrl+D) to view the masked channel; optionally repeat for the TH channel.

steps.title: Detect Citrine+ cells (spot detection)
steps.instruction: Open the Spots wizard (3D view > Spots). Choose the non‑masked Citrine channel. Estimate the XY diameter as 6 µm (measure a few cells). Deselect ‘Model PSF‑elongation along Z’. Enable ‘Background Subtraction’. Set filters: Quality > 300, Intensity max > 1500 (masked channel), Mean intensity > 1000 (masked channel). Run the wizard to create spots.

steps.title: Export spot coordinates
steps.instruction: In the Spots menu, go to Statistics > Detailed > Position Reference Frame. Export the table to .xls or .csv. The file contains X, Y, Z distances of each spot relative to the reference frame.

steps.title: Measure axis lengths for binning
steps.instruction: Create a new Spot object, choose ‘Skip automatic creation, edit manually’, then in the Edit tab select ‘Surface of Object’. Place a spot on the most lateral (or rostral, or ventral) point of the TH surface (Shift+left click). Use Statistics > Position Reference Frame to read the coordinate value. Repeat for each axis to obtain total length for bin division.

steps.title: Optional: Group and colour‑code bins
steps.instruction: In the Spots Filter tab, add a filter for Position X (or Y, Z) Reference Frame. Define upper and lower thresholds for each bin (e.g., 8 medio‑lateral bins between midline and most lateral point). Click ‘Duplicate Selection to new Spots’ for each bin. Gather all bin Spot objects into a folder (3D view > Group) and assign a unique colour via the Color tab. Repeat for dorso‑ventral and rostro‑caudal axes. (Since Imaris 9.6, the ‘Classify spots’ function can create all groups at once.)
